verses.zh: （上行之诗。）凡敬畏耶和华、遵行他道的人便为有福！
verses.en: A song of ascents.[NOTE:1] How blessed is every one of the Lord’s loyal followers,[NOTE:2] each one who keeps his commands.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 128. The psalmist observes that the godly individual has genuine happiness because the Lord rewards such a person with prosperity and numerous children.

The precise significance of this title, which appears in Pss 120-134, is unclear. Perhaps worshipers recited these psalms when they ascended the road to Jerusalem to celebrate annual religious festivals. For a discussion of their background see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 219-21.
verses.commentary:
128:1 "blessed" See note on this word (BDB 80) at Ps. 1:1. There are two major terms in Hebrew for the concept of
"blessed" or "happy," both relating to God and humans. Let me use Deuteronomy 33 as an example.

- bless (see SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING [OT])

- NOUN ‒ BDB 139, cf. Deut. 33:23

- VERB ‒ BDB 138, cf. Deut. 33:1,13,20,24

- bless ‒ BDB 80, used in Ps. 1:1 and 18 more times in Psalms but not in Genesis or Deuteronomy

YHWH's blessings are directly related to those covered by His covenant. It is based on obedience (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP). This whole concept
of prosperity and contentment is part of the OT's "two ways," seen in Psalm 1; Deut. 30:15,19 and described as "cursing"
and "blessing" in Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-30.

The truly blessed person is the one who is rightly related to (1) God, (2) his/her family, and
(3) the people of God. All three spheres must be in harmony!

▣ "everyone" Notice how this is limited (similar to Romans 8:28).

- those who fear the Lord, Ps. 128:3,4 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR [OT])

- those who walk in His ways (cf. Ps. 119:2-3)

So the blessing is not for "everyone," not even for all covenant people, but only for faithful followers!

This has implications on how Christians should view the modern state of Israel. Covenant obedience
is a prerequisite to covenant promises!

▣ "fears" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

▣ "Who walks" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "ways" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

verses.zh: 你要吃劳碌得来的；你要享福，事情顺利。
verses.en: You[NOTE:1] will eat what you worked so hard to grow.[NOTE:2] You will be blessed and secure.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the one who walks in his ways.”

The psalmist addresses the representative God-fearing man, as indicated by the references to “your wife” (v. 3) and “the man” (v. 4), as well as the second masculine singular pronominal and verbal forms in vv. 2-6.
Heb “the work of your hands, indeed you will eat.”
verses.commentary:
128:2-3 Notice the covenant promises for faithful followers (here, to one individual).

- enjoy the fruit of their labors

- be happy

- good life

- good home life

- many, healthy children

- a long life

This is the essence of OT blessings. YHWH wanted to get the attention of the nations by blessing
Israel. Once they noticed, Israel was to share the source of their blessing and peace—YHWH.

It should be stated that abundant population growth was a command of God in

- Gen. 1:28; 9:1,7

- it was part of the promise to Abraham in Gen. 12:2; 13:16; 16:10

- it was also the reality of the family of Jacob (cf. Gen. 28:14) in Egypt that caused the Egyptian leaders to
fear and persecute Israel (Exodus 1-2).

128:2a Just a note to mention that this promise is the exact opposite of the threat of exile! The exiles
were God's judgment on faithless covenant followers. It was the very opposite of His intended purposes. It was
the epitome of irony!

verses.zh: 你妻子在你的内室，好像多结果子的葡萄树；你儿女围绕你的桌子，好像橄榄栽子。
verses.en: Your wife will be like a fruitful vine[NOTE:1] in the inner rooms of your house;your children[NOTE:2] will be like olive branches,as they sit all around your table.
notes: Heb “how blessed you [will be] and it will be good for you.”
The metaphor of the fruitful vine pictures the wife as fertile; she will give her husband numerous children (see the next line).

verses.zh: 看哪，敬畏耶和华的人必要这样蒙福！
verses.en: Yes indeed, the man who fears the Lordwill be blessed in this way.[NOTE:1]
notes: One could translate “sons” (see Ps 127:3 and the note on the word “sons” there), but here the term seems to refer more generally to children of both genders.

verses.zh: 愿耶和华从锡安赐福给你！愿你一生一世看见耶路撒冷的好处！
verses.en: May the Lord bless you[NOTE:1] from Zionthat you might see[NOTE:2] Jerusalem[NOTE:3] prosperall the days of your life
notes: Heb “look, indeed thus will the man, the fearer of the Lord, be blessed.”

The prefixed verbal form is understood as a jussive of prayer (note the imperatives that are subordinated to this clause in vv. 5b-6a). Having described the blessings that typically come to the godly, the psalmist concludes by praying that this ideal may become reality for the representative godly man being addressed.
The imperative with prefixed vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding jussive.
verses.commentary:
128:5-6 This is a closing prayer for both the individual faithful follower and national Israel (cf. Ps. 128:6b). Often
psalms started out as individuals addressing God, but in time, they turned into corporate psalms.

- Ps. 128:5a ‒ bless (BDB 138, KB 159, Piel IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense)

- Ps. 128:5b ‒ may you see. . . (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERATIVE)

- Ps. 128:6a ‒ same as #2

- Ps. 128:6b ‒ no VERB but an assumed prayer (cf. Ps. 125:5)

It is interesting that Paul's allusion to the church in Gal. 6:16 uses similar phrasing to Ps. 128:6. Whether
it is a direct, conscious allusion is uncertain.

▣ Notice that "the prosperity of Jerusalem" is parallel to "see your children's children." This refers to long
term peace, prosperity, and societal stability (i.e., "you see your children's children"), v. 6a.

128:5 "from Zion" This refers to YHWH dwelling in the temple (cf. Ps. 20:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

128:6b "Peace be upon Israel" This is a recurrent theme (cf. Ps. 125:5; Isa. 66:12). YHWH will bring world peace
(cf. Isa. 2:4; 9:5,6; Micah 4:3,4; Zech. 9:10). The Messiah will be "the Prince of Peace."

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Define the Hebrew term "blessed" (Ps. 128:1a).

- Define the Hebrew term "fear" (Ps. 128:1a).

- Why is "many children" considered a blessing?

- How are the categories of faith, home, and nation linked?

verses.en: and that you might see[NOTE:1] your grandchildren.[NOTE:2] May Israel experience peace.[NOTE:3]
